title: Why a constructor has the same name as its class
answer: Java uses the class name plus the absence of a return type to distinguish a constructor declaration from an ordinary method. This syntax ties the initialization member directly to the type being created. In AeroTopo, `Orthomosaic(...)` is recognizable as the constructor because its name exactly matches `Orthomosaic`, while `resolutionMetres()` and `copy()` are ordinary methods with return types.
